item.title: Turkey's parliament approves a pardon-like bill for thousands of PKK militants
item.description: Turkey's parliament approved legislation that would introduce a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants in a bid to advance the government's peace initiative with their insurgent group.
item.content:encoded:
Turkey's parliament approved legislation that would introduce a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants in a bid to advance the government's peace initiative with their insurgent group.

(Image credit: Metin Yoksu)

item.title: Trump pivots back to sanctions for Iran as other strategies to end his war fizzle
item.description: The shift comes as U.S. stockpiles of key weapons have dwindled and as stop-start talks seem again to have stalled. But Trump insists the pressure can lead to a breakthrough.

item.title: Magnitude 7.4 quake rocks western Colombia, killing at least 111 people
item.description: Search teams and civilians picked through the remains of destroyed buildings in the country's third-largest city, Cali, passing large pieces of concrete and rubble down a long line of volunteers.

item.title: Alabama heads into a second primary election after redistricting
item.description: Alabama voters are again selecting candidates for four Congressional districts after the state changed the district map to favor Republicans. The redistricting is causing confusion among voters.

item.title: After his Reflecting Pool vandalism case is dismissed, David Hearn looks for closure
item.description: The ex-Olympian accused of damaging the reflecting pool tells NPR the experience has been "Orwellian" and "Kafkaesque." And it's not over yet: His lawyers are fighting to close the case permanently.

item.title: Trump and RFK Jr. try again to upend vaccines for kids
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday about vaccines, saying children should get fewer. His administration has been blocked in the courts from changing the vaccine schedule.

item.title: 'The Nerd Reich' tracks the 'unmasking of Silicon Valley's true politics'
item.description: Journalist Gil Durán argues that a small circle of Silicon Valley billionaires and venture capitalists have concluded that democracy is in their way — and that they should be governing in its place.

item.title: Does spending money make you feel bad? Read this comic
item.description: If spending — or not spending — money makes you feel shame or regret, you might be grappling with financial guilt. Financial planner Lauryn Williams breaks down three types and how to deal.

item.title: Flood death toll in India's Assam reaches 100 as thousands lose their homes
item.description: Days of heavy monsoon rain has caused rivers, including the Brahmaputra, to overflow, inundating communities, disrupting livelihoods and damaging infrastructure.
